clue.text: Dance, Dance with style!

parts.note: Charles Dance is an English actor, so his surname leads to his first name
ton means fashion or style, as in 'bon ton'

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging someone to dance, and to do it with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'Dance' looks like a stutter; the second is the actor Charles Dance, giving his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively 1920s ballroom step named after a city in South Carolina.

clue.text: He is a joker

parts.note: a joker is also a playing ..., and a comical person is called by that playing-... word

explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially an amusing, eccentric person is described with the same word as a playing card.

clue.text: Two graduates come in to transform old university

indicators.note: the graduates come into the middle of the word for transform

parts.note: to alter is to transform
MA is Master of Arts, a graduate
the second MA, since there are two graduates

explanation.surface: A pair of graduates return to shake up their former college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two graduates' each give the same Master of Arts degree; 'come in to' signals the container, not arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase for 'nourishing mother' is used for the college or school one attended.

clue.text: Many a remarkable person is solitary

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many
a oner is a unique, remarkable person or thing

explanation.surface: An observation that exceptional people tend to keep to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' giving L comes from the Roman numeral 50; 'solitary' is read as a noun, a recluse.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun a solitary is a recluse, someone who lives or keeps apart from others.

clue.text: Worldly, and cruel as can be

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are shown as what they can be when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes worldliness as being as cruel as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as can be' looks like an intensifier, but 'can be' signals the anagram of CRUEL AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Secular things belong to the worldly rather than the religious or spiritual sphere.

clue.text: Fellow goes to ring grandma continually

indicators.note: the fellow goes to the end, after the other pieces

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
nan is an informal word for grandmother
a don is a college fellow

explanation.surface: A man keeps phoning his grandmother again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a telephone call but is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means without stopping, going on and on at length.

clue.text: Dog food

explanation.definitionFit: The breed is a fluffy Chinese dog, and the slang word means grub or a meal.

clue.text: Heroic writer hit during a ball game

definitions.meaning: the Greek epic poet of the Iliad and Odyssey
in baseball a home run is called by this short name

explanation.definitionFit: The Greek epic poet shares a name with baseball slang for a home run.

clue.text: Rifle a cathedral city

definitions.meaning: the American repeating rifle of the Wild West
the Hampshire city with a great medieval cathedral

explanation.definitionFit: A famous repeating rifle brand, and an English city in Hampshire with a cathedral and ancient school.

clue.text: Fish straying all over the place

indicators.note: scattered in every direction, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fish wandering aimlessly in every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges the letters of STRAYING.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat ray with a venomous barbed tail is a kind of fish.

clue.text: European capitalist is right to convert Arabian state

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A European financier is told he must convert to an Arabian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitalist' is not a financier but a resident of a capital, here Rome; 'to convert' is padding linking the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Rome lives in Italy's capital city, hence a European 'capitalist'.

clue.text: Yachting enthusiast takes in single artisan

annotationWithheld.why: Yachting enthusiast takes in single artisan: no parse found taking in a letter for 'single' to give CRAFTSMAN; likely garbled in OCR
annotationWithheld.clue: Yachting enthusiast takes in single artisan

clue.text: Bright boy installs trade centre in Laurie Lee's village

indicators.note: the market is placed inside the name of the village

parts.note: Slad is the Gloucestershire village of Cider with Rosie by Laurie Lee
a mart is a market, a centre of trade

explanation.surface: A clever lad sets up a market in a Gloucestershire village.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurie Lee's memoir Cider with Rosie is set in his Cotswold village; 'installs' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart-alec or clever young fellow; the phrase is informal British for a bright boy.

clue.text: Pole who became Prime Minister of England

definitions.text: who became Prime Minister of England
definitions.meaning: Lord ... was British Prime Minister during the American War of Independence

explanation.definitionFit: One of the two geographic poles, and the surname of Lord North, eighteenth-century British premier.

clue.text: Star is paid outrageously for a pot plant

indicators.note: behaving wildly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A celebrity is overpaid for a houseplant.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardy leafy houseplant beloved of Victorian parlours.

clue.text: Established bazaar likely to succeed

parts.note: set means fixed or established
a fair is a bazaar or market

explanation.surface: A well-established market looks set for success.
explanation.definitionFit: Of weather or prospects, settled and promising a good outcome.

clue.text: Governess with inclination to be a historian

parts.note: Anna Leonowens was the governess of The King and I
a list is a tilt or lean

explanation.surface: A governess with a bent for scholarship becomes a chronicler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclination' looks like a preference but is a ship's lean.
explanation.definitionFit: One who records events year by year writes annals, a kind of history.

clue.text: Managed to put over arguments that are sound

indicators.note: the word for managed is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: ran means managed
rows are quarrels

explanation.surface: Someone managed to win sound arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective but is a noun, a strait.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow channel of water between landmasses, like a sound or strait.

clue.text: About one thousand leguminous plants produce spontaneously

parts.note: on means about, concerning
I is the Roman numeral one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
pulses are peas, beans and lentils

explanation.surface: Bean plants by the thousand appear without planning.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without forethought, suddenly and by whim.

clue.text: Earning settlement can now be reached

indicators.note: a settlement rearranges matters, so the letters are resettled

explanation.surface: A wage deal is finally within reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' looks like a pay deal but rearranges EARNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Within reach or distance of a target, as for a gun or transmitter.

clue.text: Egyptian faces a strict oriental

indicators.note: the Egyptian faces the rest, coming before them

parts.note: E is an abbreviation for Egyptian
stern means strict

explanation.surface: An Egyptian confronts a stern Asian person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean belonging to or from the East.

clue.text: Cable made from bales is crazy

definitions.meaning: wire used for binding bales of hay
going wild or out of control

explanation.definitionFit: Baling wire is literally the wire for hay, and the slang sense is out of control or erratic.

clue.text: Principal determined to provide earphones

parts.note: a head is a principal
set means determined, resolved

explanation.surface: A headteacher decides to hand out earphones.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of earpieces joined by a band, worn for listening.

clue.text: Drive into Antrim pell-mell

indicators.note: the answer is found going into the words that follow

explanation.surface: A frantic drive into Antrim, a county of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To propel or urge forward is to drive.

clue.text: He prods people to have an iron in the fire

definitions.meaning: a metal rod for stirring a fire

explanation.definitionFit: A person who jabs others, and the fire-iron used to stir coals.

clue.text: Lady Hester's family carriage

definitions.meaning: Lady Hester ... was an aristocratic traveller in the Middle East

explanation.definitionFit: The aristocratic surname of the traveller Lady Hester, and a light two-wheeled gig named after a clergyman.

clue.text: Czechoslovakia's own Liberal leader

parts.note: to have is to own

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word Liberal

explanation.surface: Czechoslovakia has its own leader from the Liberals.
explanation.walkthrough: Vaclav Havel was Czechoslovakia's last president; the definition reads as 'Czechoslovakia's man'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaclav Havel was the playwright who became Czechoslovakia's president in 1989.

clue.text: Sweet and sour

definitions.meaning: a pastry with a sweet filling

explanation.definitionFit: A pastry dessert, and an adjective meaning sharp-tasting; the clue plays opposites against each other.

clue.text: Walker must do something about it

definitions.text: Walker must do something about it

parts.words: Walker must do something about it
parts.note: a walker moves by footfalls, and the idiom for acting on a problem uses the same footfalls

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to act to deal with a problem; a walker literally does it.

clue.text: Heartsick Virginia is home

annotationWithheld.why: Heartsick Virginia is home: VILLA is ILL in VA, but the one word 'Heartsick' gives both ILL and the container signal, a word doing two jobs

clue.text: Gives vent to feelings in songs

definitions.meaning: to express openly, as of feelings or opinions

explanation.definitionFit: To voice opinions publicly, and a plural of tune or melody.

clue.text: Regular payment this month leads to mental breakdown

parts.note: inst. (instant) is old commercial shorthand for this month; it leads the answer

indicators.note: a breakdown breaks the word up, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: Monthly bills are driving someone to a nervous collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: INST (instant) is old business letter shorthand for 'of this month'; 'breakdown' rearranges MENTAL to ALMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: One of a series of payments spread over time.
